newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET - S.AFRICA OFF TO SOLID START VS INDIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET - S.AFRICA OFF TO SOLID START VS INDIA.

text.p: South Africa got off to a solid start on Wednesday, with openers Andrew Hudson and Gary Kirsten scoring 41 and 50, respectively, on the first day of the second test at Eden Gardens.
At lunch South Africa were 98 for no wicket.
South African skipper Hansie Cronje won the toss and chose to bat first on a wicket which turned out to be a good batting track.
Indian captain Sachin Tendulkar tried all his bowlers except leg-spinner Narendra Hirwani but failed to break the South African opening partnership.
In a surprise move, South Africa left Fanie de Villiers out of the playing 11 and handed all-rounder Lance Klusener his test debut.
De Villiers was the top scorer in the first test in Ahmedabad.
A general strike in Calcutta, which paralysed the eastern city's transport system, did not prevent at least 50,000 die-hard spectators from thronging to Eden Gardens.
Indian fast bowler Javagal Srinath maintained a good line and length but got little assistance from the wicket. He was unlucky not to get rid of Hudson.
Kirsten batted confidently and reached his half-century just before lunch. He hit seven fours in his half-century off 82 balls.
Hudson also stroked seven boundaries in his knock of 41.
